newsitem.title: USA: CME's Brodsky is candidate for NASD job - report.
newsitem.headline: CME's Brodsky is candidate for NASD job - report.

text.p: William Brodsky, president and chief executive of the Chicago Mercantile Exchange, is a candidate for the top job at the National Association of Securities Dealers (NASD), a local newspaper reported Monday.
Crain's Chicago Business said executive recruiter Korn/Ferry International has been in contact with Brodsky about the job.

The CME declined to comment on behalf of Brodsky, who has been president of the U.S. futures exchange since June 1, 1985. He joined the CME as executive vice president and chief operating officer in 1982.
Prior to joining the CME, Brodsky worked at the American Stock Exchange and was its executive vice president for operations from 1979 to 1982.

Timothy Gilles, vice president and manager of media relations at Merrill Lynch, said Daniel Tully, Merrill chairman and chairman of the NASD board of governors, was working with Korn/Ferry to select one of six candidates to replace retiring NASD president and CEO Joseph Hardiman.
Gilles would not name the candidates.
"We are not commenting on individual names," he said, adding that NASD still aimed to have a successor named before the end of the year. Hardiman's retirement date has not been set.
A spokesman at the NASD declilned to confirm or deny the reports.
Brodsky's name has also surfaced as a contender to succeed Alger "Duke" Chapman, Chicago Board Options Exchange chairman and CEO. Chapman's contract expires in mid-1997.
On Monday, both Crain's and the Chicago Tribune reiterated industry speculation that Brodsky was under consideration for Chapman's job.

Neither the CBOE nor Russell Reynolds Associates Inc, the CBOE's headhunter, would comment on talk that Brodsky was under consideration for the post. -Derivatives desk 312-408-8750;E-mail derivatives@reuters.com
